scenario: Alterion 系统设计，聊到一个超热门 key 的缓存到期，成千上万个请求同一瞬间 miss、全砸向数据库。你想说「加一把锁或给个短宽限期，别让缓存击穿打垮数据库」，上一轮却卡成 “when the cache is is empty, everyone go to the database”。
scenario_en: In an Alterion system-design round, a super-hot key's cache entry expires and thousands of requests miss at the same instant, all slamming the DB together. Last time you stalled at "when the cache is is empty, everyone go to the database."
q: 「缓存同一时刻失效，大量请求同时回源打崩数据库，得靠锁或短宽限期兜住」这一句怎么说地道？
q_en: How do you name "a cache stampede — everything misses at once and hammers the DB, so we add a lock or a short grace TTL"?
options: When the cache is is empty at the same time, everyone go to the database together and it get really slow.
We'd hit a cache stampede — thousands of requests miss at once, so we add a lock or a short grace TTL.
So so when it expires, when the the cache expires, everyone everyone hits the database at once, at once...
A cache stampede transpires when numerous concurrent requests simultaneously access the origin database upon expiration.
tradeoff: 地道术语 cache stampede + 一句锁/宽限期的补救 vs 直译“is is empty”或绕圈子：前者一句话点名现象并给出防护，后者暴露术语不熟。
why: 术语是 cache stampede（也叫 thundering herd）；再补一句加锁或给短宽限期，就证明你懂怎么防止请求一拥而上打崩数据库。
why_en: It's a cache stampede, also called thundering herd — then "a lock or a short grace TTL" shows you know the fix, not just the word.
whenOtherWins: 如果这个 key 冷门、并发量本来就小，直接说 "a miss just refetches" 也够，不必上锁或宽限期。
options_en: When the cache is is empty at the same time, everyone go to the database together and it get really slow.
We'd hit a cache stampede — thousands of requests miss at once, so we add a lock or a short grace TTL.
So so when it expires, when the the cache expires, everyone everyone hits the database at once, at once...
A cache stampede transpires when numerous concurrent requests simultaneously access the origin database upon expiration.

反复 “so so / everyone everyone” 打转，没收尾。
用 “transpires…simultaneously…upon” 的书面腔念定义。

Names the problem and gives the lock/TTL fix.
Loops on "so so / everyone everyone," never lands.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个热点 key 的缓存同时失效，大量请求同一瞬间 miss、一起回源打数据库的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache stampede (thundering herd) is when a hot key's cache entry expires and a flood of requests miss at once, all hitting the DB together.

termDefinitions.meaning: 到期后仍短暂放行旧值、只让一个请求去刷新的宽限期，避免所有请求一起回源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A grace TTL keeps serving the stale value for a short window while only one request refreshes it, so the rest don't all hit the DB.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存刷新时加的锁，只放一个请求去查库，其余请求等待或先拿旧值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A refresh lock lets only one request go query the DB on a miss; the rest wait or get served the stale value.

scenario: Alterion 面试问怎么加速热点查询。你上一轮说 “have some cache put in Redis, something like that” 就停了，没讲清「命中直接返回，miss 才回源查库再写回」。
scenario_en: An Alterion interviewer asks how you'd speed up hot reads. Last time you trailed off at "have some cache put in Redis, something like that" without explaining hit vs. miss.
q: 「先查缓存，命中就返回，miss 就回源查库再写回缓存」这套 cache-aside 怎么说？
q_en: How do you say the cache-aside read path — check cache, return on hit, fall back and repopulate on a miss?
options: We check the cache first; on a miss we fall back to the DB and populate the cache.
We put some cache in Redis, so like when we query it's faster, something like that.
So we we look in the cache, and if it's not there, not there, we go to the, to the database, and then we put it back...
Upon a cache miss the system retrieves the record from the database and subsequently repopulates the cache.
tradeoff: 用 hit / miss / populate 三个术语讲完 cache-aside vs “put some cache in Redis” 含糊带过：前者证明你懂回源与写回，后者只报了个存储名。
why: 关键是 cache hit / cache miss 加“回源查库再写回”：一句话把命中返回和 miss 回源都讲了，这才是 cache-aside。
why_en: Say cache hit and cache miss plus "fall back to the DB and populate the cache" — that one line is the whole cache-aside read path.
whenOtherWins: 对方已在聊命中率细节时，可直接跳到 "our hit rate is around 95%"，不必从头讲 cache-aside 流程。
options_en: We check the cache first; on a miss we fall back to the DB and populate the cache.
We put some cache in Redis, so like when we query it's faster, something like that.
So we we look in the cache, and if it's not there, not there, we go to the, to the database, and then we put it back...
Upon a cache miss the system retrieves the record from the database and subsequently repopulates the cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 要的数据在缓存里叫命中(hit)，不在、得回源查库叫未命中(miss)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache hit is when the data is already in the cache; a cache miss is when it isn't and you go to the source.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用先查缓存，miss 时自己回源查库再把结果写回缓存的模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache-aside means the app checks the cache, and on a miss it reads the DB and writes the result back into the cache itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把回源查到的数据写进缓存，下次好命中；也说 warm the cache。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To populate the cache is to write the fetched data into it so the next read hits; also called warming the cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存命中率：命中次数占总请求的比例，衡量缓存效果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hit rate is the share of requests served from cache — the main measure of how well the cache is working.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库，缓存 miss 时回源查的权威数据源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DB is the database — the source of truth you fall back to on a cache miss.

scenario: Alterion 追问：缓存怎么保证不返回过期数据？你想说「给缓存设个过期时间，到点自动失效」，但一时想不起 TTL 这个词，差点绕着描述。
scenario_en: The Alterion interviewer asks how the cache avoids serving stale data. You want to say "set an expiry so entries drop on their own," but the word TTL slips and you nearly describe around it.
q: 「给缓存设 TTL，到期自动失效，避免返回脏数据」这一句怎么地道说？
q_en: How do you say "set a TTL so the entry expires and we don't serve stale data"?
options: We set a time, so the data will be out of date after a while, and then it gets deleted.
So we we give it a time, a time limit, and when the time, when the time is up, it's not valid...
A time-to-live parameter is configured such that the cached entry is invalidated upon expiration.
We set a short TTL so the entry expires on its own, so we don't serve stale data.
tradeoff: TTL / expire / stale 术语 vs “set a time... out of date” 绕着说：前者点名机制并说清它防的问题，后者听着像不熟缓存术语。
why: 术语是 TTL（time to live）+ 动词 expire + “serve stale data”——一句话既交代到期失效，又点出它防的是返回脏数据。
why_en: It's TTL plus "expires" plus "serve stale data" — one line gives both the expiry and the problem it prevents.
codeSample:
# Redis: cache the value with a 60-second TTL
SET user:42 "{...}" EX 60
# EX 60 = expire after 60s; the key drops itself, no stale read
TTL user:42   # -> seconds left before it expires
whenOtherWins: 若一致性要求很高、必须写时主动失效而不是等到期，就该说 "we invalidate the key on write"，靠 TTL 兜底不够。

So we we give it a time, a time limit, and when the time, when the time is up, it's not valid...
A time-to-live parameter is configured such that the cached entry is invalidated upon expiration.
We set a short TTL so the entry expires on its own, so we don't serve stale data.

反复 “we we / when the time” 打转，句子散了。
用 “configured such that / upon” 的书面腔念定义。
TTL 到期自动 expire，避免返回 stale 数据。

termDefinitions.meaning: 存活时间：给缓存条目设的过期时长，到点自动失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL, Time To Live, is the lifespan you set on a cache entry — it expires automatically when the time is up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 已经过期、和源数据不一致的旧数据；返回它叫 serve stale data。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Stale data is cached data that's out of date versus the source; returning it is called serving stale data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主动把缓存条目标记失效（通常写时触发），区别于等 TTL 到期。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To invalidate is to actively mark a cache entry dead — usually on a write — as opposed to waiting for TTL expiry.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内存满时按最久未用踢掉条目，叫 evict；和到期 expire 是两回事。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eviction drops entries when memory is full — LRU throws out the least recently used — which is different from TTL expiry.

scenario: 系统设计里聊到某个明星用户的 key 被疯狂读，压垮了一台节点。你想描述这个「热点 key」问题和「复制到多节点分摊」的解法，但没找到 hot key 这个词。
scenario_en: Mid system-design, one celebrity's key is getting hammered and it's overloading a single node. You want to name the hot-key problem and the replicate-across-nodes fix, but the term hot key won't come.
q: 「单个热点 key 打爆一台分片，得复制到多个节点分摊读」这一句怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "one hot key overloads a single shard, so we replicate it across nodes to spread the read load"?
options: There is like a very popular key, and it's queried a lot, so one machine gets, gets very busy.
One hot key hammers a single shard, so we replicate it across a few nodes to spread the load.
So so this key, this one key, it's read so many, so many times, and the one node, it kind of can't handle...
A single frequently-accessed key induces excessive load upon one shard, necessitating replication.
tradeoff: hot key / shard / replicate 术语 vs “one machine gets busy” 白描：前者证明你懂分片被热点拖累的机制，后者听不出问题在哪。
why: 术语是 hot key + “hammers a single shard” + “replicate across nodes”——一句话点出热点打爆单分片，以及靠复制分摊读的解法。
why_en: It's hot key plus "hammers a single shard" plus "replicate across nodes" — that names the problem and the fix in one breath.
whenOtherWins: 若热点是写而不是读，复制副本救不了热点写；那时该说 "we shard the key itself" 或加本地缓存/合并写。

termDefinitions.meaning: 被访问量远高于其他 key 的热点键，容易把它所在的单个节点/分片压垮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot key is one key getting far more traffic than the rest, enough to overload the single node or shard that holds it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据水平切分后的一个分片；每个 key 通常只落在一个分片上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shard is one horizontal partition of the data; a given key usually lives on just one shard.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把同一个热点 key 复制到多个节点，让读请求分摊到副本上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To replicate is to copy the same hot key onto several nodes so reads spread across the copies.
